edits.old: Atlas warns that mongodb.atlas.replstatus.health can remain healthy when nodes stop sending pings, or become inaccurate during partitions and Datadog ingestion problems. Configure no-data monitoring rather than treating health=1 alone as proof of availability. (low confidence)
edits.new: Atlas warns that mongodb.atlas.replstatus.health can be inaccurate: if all nodes are unresponsive and no new pings arrive, Datadog can keep reporting them as healthy, and during network partitions or a Datadog ingestion outage or slowdown the value can be wrong. If the health status is 1 but no other metrics appear in Datadog, the replica set might be down. Atlas also documents Datadog no-data alerts, which notify you when a metric is not reporting data and help identify issues with the integration. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md

evidence.quote: If all nodes are unresponsive or their state is hanging, no new pings come in. The Atlas UI reports these nodes as down, but Datadog reports them as healthy and the status gets older.
If Datadog experiences an outage or slowdown in metrics ingestion, this metric may report incorrectly and produce a false positive result.
IMPORTANT: If the health status is `1`, but no other metrics appear in Datadog, the replica set might be down.
This feature helps you identify issues with your Atlas integration such as changes in performance, API Key issues, or broken connections.
